messages:
maya: Heads up — we saw a sustained p99 increase on /v1/generate for the last 45m, coincides with a traffic spike and a couple of customer tool-call flows. p99 ~1.8s (baseline ~600ms).
jon: I started a quick trace. Looks like a subset of requests jump to seq_len ~6k due to long user prompt + tool metadata. that forces fallback to slow kernel.
sven: Are those tool-calls expanding prompts inline or happening as separate calls?
maya: They're inline. Customer sends a long prompt, then we do a tool call that returns structured content and we append it — ends up with huge context for the final generation.
li: Perf highlights: kernel selection currently picks kernel_A up to 2k tokens, kernel_B beyond that. kernel_B has worse latency for short generations due to different memory pattern (we saw >2x latency at seq_len 6k).
jon: I captured a small profile for one of the slow traces:
```
# LR debug slice
request_id: r-1a2b3c
model: opt-13b
seq_in: 6200
microbatch: 4
chosen_kernel: kernel_B
gpu_busy_ms: 420
gpu_idle_ms: 120
kv_evictions: 3
```
li: Also saw repeated KV cache thrash. Tool-call loop causes multiple cache flushes: we set cache key per conversation chunk and the post-tool append invalidates previous prefix cached entries.
sven: That explains tail spikes — flushing KV for long context causes re-sent kv loads and kernel memory traffic.
maya: Any evidence of batching heuristics contributing?
jon: Yes. With microbatch size 4 and our batching window 10ms, the controller tries to pack but because some requests have huge seq_len they block the batch, delaying other small requests. So throughput optimized path increases tail for latency-sensitive ones.
li: TL;DR causality: long prompt + inline tool append -> seq_len bump -> kernel_B selection + KV cache eviction -> single request holds GPU for long -> microbatching holds small requests behind it -> p99 spike.
perf-bot: perf/regression: suspected 2.1% increase in p99 for /v1/generate after recent kernel-selection changes. See: https://perf.internal/runs/2026-03-16/7643
maya: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) detect tool-call append patterns and route those to dedicated throughput lane; 2) cap microbatch contribution per-request (fast-path-preempt); 3) pre-warm/avoid KV evictions for known long-context flows; 4) adjust kernel-selection threshold algorithm to consider expected generated tokens not just input seq_len.
sven: We should also consider early-routing to a slow-path queue that uses bigger microbatch and no head-of-line blocking for latency-sensitive small requests.
jon: Put another way: separate latency vs throughput lanes plus smarter kernel pick — but need a short-term hotfix.
li: Short-term patch proposal (can be deployable as config tweak):
```
# config snippet
routes:
  - match: /v1/generate
    heuristics:
      tool_call_append_detect: true
      seq_len_limit_for_fastkernel: 2048  # lower threshold until we rebench
      max_microbatch_hold_per_request_ms: 50
      kv_prewarm: true
```
maya: I like that. max_microbatch_hold_per_request_ms would let a long-running request be preempted for N ms to let small ones through, right?
li: Exactly — it's cooperative yielding in the microbatch loop. Implementation: check elapsed on request, if > threshold, push to backlog and proceed with next. Minimal infra change.
jon: Risk: yields can hurt throughput. We'll gate behind a feature flag and enable for the customer experiencing the issue and internal canary.
sven: For medium-term: reprofile kernel_B, see if we can optimize for skewed short-generations-in-long-seq scenarios. Also add kernel scoring that uses (input_seq + expected_output) rather than just input_seq.
maya: Who can own the immediate rollout? I can do config + canary. jon can add detection logic, li can implement preempt in microbatch loop. sven will take kernel re-eval.
jon: I'll open a PR with the append-detect heuristic and a unit test covering tool-call patterns.
li: I'll prototype the microbatch yield in a branch, add a perf-test harness.
sven: I'll bench kernels on synthetic dataset: long-prefix + short-gen, long-prefix + long-gen, toolcalls. Expect to publish numbers by EOD.
maya: Good. For observability: add a tag to spans "tool-append" and emit kernel_choice + kv_eviction_count in logs so we can filter tail traces easily.
perf-bot: note: flagging a regression ticket: PERF-1129. Assign to eng-runtime on call.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: eng-runtime/patch/tool-append-detect -> canary @ us-west-2, 5% traffic in 30m.
maya: Cool. Let's reconvene in 90m with initial canary results and perf numbers. :thumbsup:
jon: adding test cases now.
li: starting prototype.
sven: bench run kicked off.
maya: thanks all — big win if we can keep latency lane predictable without sacrificing throughput.
